title: Investigating a sudden p99 latency increase (synthetic demo rubric, not validated)

criteria.description: Establishes the scope from metrics first: when it started, which endpoints, regions or tenants are affected, and whether the median moved too.
Correlates the increase with recent changes: deployments, configuration, traffic or dependencies.
Uses tracing and profiling to find where the time goes: distributed traces, flame graphs, slow query logs.
Considers causes specific to the tail: garbage collection pauses, lock contention, queueing, noisy neighbours, cold caches, retries.
Limits the impact (rollback, scaling, shedding load) before or while the root cause is found.
Reasons from evidence and says how each hypothesis would be confirmed or ruled out.

references.title: Site Reliability Engineering: Monitoring Distributed Systems
references.summary: Monitor latency, traffic, errors and saturation; distinguish symptoms from causes and look at the distribution, not only the mean.

references.title: Dean and Barroso, The Tail at Scale
references.summary: Rare slow components dominate tail latency at scale; causes include queueing, shared resources, background activity and garbage collection.
